- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending upward, model frequently overestimates near-term gains; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average to prevent runaway bias.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6); add 1–2% upward bias in the 10–15 day horizon to reflect sentiment-driven reversion.
- In low-sentiment environments, model often lags behind true price by 2–5 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with a 1–2% upward adjustment to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.2 in 3-day window), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 day moving average to reduce false peaks.
